summary: Douglas County, OR ground lookout: an L-5 cab from 1933 (one source says L-4), staffed in 1941, removed or destroyed in 1962; remnants remain on the ridge.

facts.design: L-5 cab (1933) per the Register and Firelookout.com; Oregon Lookouts lists an FC-2 (L-4) house around 1934 with question marks
facts.status_note: Cab removed or destroyed in 1962 (sources differ on which); Mountain Plants of the Western Cascades describes remnants of the old lookout

staffing.status: staffed 75 days in 1941; no later staffing in the sources read

access.note: Western Cascades directions run along forest roads to a pulloff, then a walk up the ridge

visit.trail_note: The old lookout site is about a quarter mile from the road, reached on foot up the ridge

corrections.why: The Register and Firelookout.com both describe an L-5 cab from 1933; the L-4 figure traces to a c.1934 plan entry that Oregon Lookouts marks with question marks
Western Cascades gives roadside directions and a walk up the ridge to the remnants of the lookout

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two sources give an L-5 cab in 1933; Oregon Lookouts gives an FC-2 (L-4) plan around 1934 with question marks. The story reports the L-5 cab and mentions the other entry.
The Register says the cab was removed in 1962 and Firelookout.com says destroyed in 1962. Both agree on the year.
The Register and Firelookout.com say Umpqua National Forest; the Oregon Lookouts heading says Willamette National Forest. The story does not name the forest.

notes_for_editor: The 1933 cab and the 1962 end are consistent across three sources, but the design (L-5 vs L-4) and the forest name disagree. The 1980 NGS-style survey description calls the house now abandoned, which does not fit a 1962 removal; the page does not say whether a building still stood then. Two correction proposals (design L-4 to L-5, access unknown to public) are for the editor to accept or reject. No photos added: no image URLs were available from the pages read. Staffing is only the 1941 season; later staffing is not in the sources read. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story now says the 1928 packer was going to drag logs (the source says he was to), and drops the unsupported 'short walk' wording.
